specification.problem: Implement a two-outcome qubit generalized measurement with Kraus operators M0=U0 diag(a,b) V and M1=U1 diag(sqrt(1-a^2),sqrt(1-b^2)) V as a Naimark dilation on one system qubit and one probe qubit, using a Z⊗Y-type interaction (controlled-RY), and check outcome probabilities and post-measurement states against the target.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single-shot dilation (N=1) on 2 qubits for a tiny explicit instance (e.g. a=0.9, b=0.5, chosen U0, U1, V). An optional N-step version with N fresh probes uses N+1 qubits. The proof that only two singular values arise, and the full decomposition of an arbitrary qubit measurement into a sequence of such steps, are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: probe RY angles conditioned on system Z-basis state 0 or 1

equations.label: Kraus operators
equations.description: Target two-outcome measurement from the sketch, with polar/singular value decomposition.
equations.justification: Taken from the method sketch; the abstract only mentions generalized measurements with two distinct singular values.
assumptions: Both operators share the right unitary V

equations.label: Angle choice
equations.description: Controlled RY angles so that the probe's |0> amplitude equals the singular value for each Z-basis state of s.

equations.label: Interaction
equations.description: Constant Z⊗Y coupling yields a controlled rotation of the probe, with opposite signs for z=0,1. Local pulses (e.g. an X on the probe or a system Z-basis flip) give the general (theta0,theta1).
equations.justification: Since Z is diagonal, the exponential splits into Z-conditioned Y rotations.
assumptions: Reaching theta0!=±theta1 needs extra pulses, which are not specified here

equations.label: Dilated circuit
equations.description: Net effect of V, controlled-RY on p, then probe-controlled U_k on s (U_0 when p=0, U_1 when p=1), implemented as controlled gates.
equations.justification: Direct computation: the p=0 amplitude is diag(cos(theta_z/2)) V psi, and the p=1 amplitude is diag(sin(theta_z/2)) V psi, up to sign conventions.
assumptions: Only the control of U_k from p=k is used, so the controls are CU1 after an X on p

equations.label: Outcome probability
equations.description: Readout comparison with the target: probe statistics and conditional system state.
assumptions: Statevector used in place of tomography

registers.name: p
registers.role: probe/ancilla qubit (qubit 1), starts in |0>, read into one classical bit

specification.initial_state: |psi>_s ⊗ |0>_p, with psi a chosen test state prepared with standard gates

steps.description: Apply CRY(theta0) on p controlled on s=0 (X on s, CRY, X on s) and CRY(theta1) on p controlled on s=1.
Apply U0 on s controlled on p=0 and U1 on s controlled on p=1 (X on p around the controlled gate for k=0); then measure p only if counts are requested, otherwise read the statevector.
Compare probe probabilities and the conditional s state with the target Kraus predictions.

specification.measurement: Measure p into classical bit 0 (Qiskit little-endian: the last character of the counts key is bit 0). Skip the measurement for statevector checks.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute p_k from counts or the statevector and compare with <psi|M_k†M_k|psi>. Compare the conditional s state via the reduced statevector given p=k.
assumptions: The choice of a, b, U0, U1, V and psi is an illustrative tiny instance
N=1 only; the continuous N-step splitting is not constructed
No black box or query is used
Qubit count 2, within a typical cap
missing_information: The proof that the composition of constant-H interactions with arbitrary unitaries yields only two singular values
The paper's exact pulse sequence and Hamiltonian normalization
The decomposition of a general qubit POVM into a sequence of such steps
The N-step small-rotation scheme with fresh probes
